newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - June 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - June 12.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents.
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- COMPUTER CHIEF GIVEN PROPERTY IN LIEU OF BONUS

The founder of the Akhter computer group, which is to be floated this month in an issue which is expected to value the company at 60 million stg, has been paying himself bonuses in buildings over the past five years. Pakistani-born Mumayun Mughal said the move was "to save National Insurance". He also admitted to paying interest and back-dated tax on expenses for which he was unable to account following an inquiry by Inland Revenue three years ago.
-- ARGOS PRICE FALLS AFTER ANALYSTS' DOWNGRADE

Shares in catalogue retailing group Argos fell 20.5p to 575p on Wednesday as investors became jittery following the downgrading of Argos profit forecasts by several analysts. Argos has issued two profit warnings this year, but finance director Bob Stewart expressed surprise at the market reaction. He said the group would be announcing interim results on August 18, when it would talk about current trading, and that the market could then make its own decisions based on "up-to-date knowledge".
-- GALEN FOUNDER GIVES 17M STG SHARES TO STAFF

The chairman and founder of Galen Holdings, the Northern Ireland-based pharmaceuticals group, is to give 17 million stg worth of shares in the group to its staff and to Queen's University, Belfast. The move by Allen McClay comes as the group prepares for a 180 million stg floatation, and will leave him with 47 percent of the company. McClay founded Galen in 1968 after working as a pharmacist for Glaxo for 13 years.
THE TIMES
-- ROBINSON CALLS FOR SHAKE-UP OF ITV NETWORK

The chairman of Granada has called for reform of the structure of the independent television network ITV. Gerry Robinson said that the current regime, in which ownership is limited to a maximum of 15 percent of the total television audience, was "ludicrous and costly", and predicted that the network would ultimately be controlled by just one media player. He said reform was necessary to allow ITV to compete with other UK broadcasters.
-- GRANT GETS EXTRA 1.8 MILLION STG

Sir Alastair Grant, the former chairman of supermarket chain Safeway, has been given 510,480 shares as part of a long-term incentive plan for executive directors. At current prices the shares are worth 1.84 million stg, and follow the award of some 382,860 shares in May. The payments relate to performance achieved in the period between April 1994 and March 1997.
-- JAPANESE PROSECUTORS RAID RETAILER'S HEADQUARTERS

Japanese retailing chain Jusco Co has seen its headquarters raided by Toyko prosecutors just 24 hours after the company's president was arrested in connection with a racketeer scandal. Jusco, which is Japan's third biggest supermarket operator in terms of sales, and which holds a 15 percent interest in UK fashion and fabrics retailer Laura Ashley, is not itself implicated in the inquiries. However, the events have tarnished its image and led to a fall in the price of its stock in Tokyo.
THE GUARDIAN
-- FREE SHARES AN ILLUSION, SAYS NATIONWIDE

The Nationwide, now Britain's biggest building society following the floatation of the Halifax, has warned that "free shares" are an illusion. Announcing pre-tax profits of 264.8 million stg, compared to 395.6 million stg the previous year, Nationwide also criticised its banking competitors for racing to increase their mortgage rates.
-- REGULATOR TURNS FIRE ON TRAIN FIRMS

Rail regulator John Swift has ordered train companies and station operators to improve service standards or face the prospect of substantial fines. Continuing his tough new approach to the industry, Swift said Wednesday that he has told operators to ensure that services provided a "seamless national network" promoting competition and co-operation for passengers.
-- DIXONS AVOIDS WARRANTY TAX BY GIVING SHOPPERS NEW KIND OF COVER

High street electrical retailer Dixons has found a way to bypass the higher rate insurance premium tax (IPT) on its product warranties. The new 17.5 percent rate on the warranties was announced in the last Budget from Chancellor Kenneth Clarke, an increase from 2.5 percent. However, Dixons has reacted by offering service contracts, which are not classified as insurance policies and so do not attract the 17.5 percent IPT.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- GOVERNMENT SEEKS UNION ADVICE ON WINDFALL TAX PITFALLS

Unison, Britain's largest union, has been approached by the government to offer advice on how to prevent privatised utilities cutting costs in order to pay the proposed windfall tax. The union, which has 1.3 million members, offered proposals ranging from outright compulsion through to persuasion via tax breaks. Unison also told the government that full protection for employees against windfall-tax related redundancies would require special provision in the legislation.
-- OFTEL PUSHES TO KEEP PHONE BAN

Telecommunications industry regulator Don Cruickshank is reported to have advised the Department of Trade and Industry that the ban which prevents British Telecom from broadcasting entertainment down its phone network cannot be lifted unilaterally without a much broader and more lengthy review of broadcasting policy. The Oftel submission casts doubt on the strength of BT's "special relationship" with the new government, which had indicated the ban could be lifted in exchange for BT connecting schools and libraries to the Internet for free.
-- IONICA SET FOR 625 MILLION STG FLOAT TO DO BATTLE WITH BT

Radio-based telecommunications group Ionica is seeking a stock market floatation next month that will value the business at 625 million stg. Ionica, which was formed five years ago, is constructing a domestic telephone network based on innovative radio technology which it hopes will compete against British Telecom. The company hopes to attract investors in part due to the very low capital expenditure of setting up its infrastructure.
